title: Sherry Gottlieb
dek_or_short_description: Bookstore owner, friend, and advocate. Operated the Change of Hobbit Bookstore in Westwood/Berkeley. Connected PKD with film and media opportunities.
body_markdown:
Sherry Gottlieb owned the Change of Hobbit Bookstore in Westwood/Berkeley during the 1970s, a venue where science fiction readers and writers gathered. She was more than a bookseller; she was an advocate for PKD's work and a friend willing to use her connections on his behalf.

PKD attended events at her store, autographing books and meeting readers. More importantly, Gottlieb was instrumental in connecting Dick with film producers and media figures interested in adapting his work. In the tumultuous years of the break-in investigation and the early aftermath of 2-3-74, she provided a stable professional relationship and a tangible reminder that his work had readers who cared.

The correspondence with Gottlieb reflects a warmer, more grounded dynamic than some of PKD's other relationships. She was a practical ally — someone who could move books, arrange meetings, and offer the kind of professional support that a literary agent provides but with genuine personal warmth.

In the broader ecology of PKD's life, figures like Gottlieb matter enormously. They are the bridge between the isolated writer and the community of readers and professionals who sustain literary careers. The bookstore itself has long since closed, but her role in advocating for PKD's work during a critical period deserves remembering.
summary: Sherry Gottlieb (1970s), bookstore owner and advocate. Operated Change of Hobbit Bookstore; connected PKD with film/media opportunities; provided professional and personal support.
